title: A Multi-level Compiler Backend for Accelerated Micro-kernels Targeting RISC-V ISA Extensions
problem: Micro-kernels for DNNs must exploit specialized hardware (custom ISA, hardware loops, streaming registers) to achieve peak performance, but classical compiler backends use CPU-focused abstractions and general-purpose heuristics, missing domain-specific optimization opportunities.
motivation: Modern accelerators have specialized hardware (loops, streaming) requiring tailored code generation; general-purpose LLVM/GCC backends cannot fully exploit these features.
method: Custom RISC-V backend with progressive lowering through multiple structured abstraction levels matching hardware capabilities. Uses incremental register allocation over structured IRs without classical spilling, enabling direct hardware loop and streaming register exploitation.
key_novelty: Breaking classical backend hourglass by progressive lowering across domain-specific abstraction levels, directly exposing hardware features like loops and streaming.
contributions: Multi-level compiler backend for RISC-V accelerators with hardware loops
Structured IR design matching accelerator capabilities
Incremental register allocation without classical spilling
Up to 90% FPU utilization on key DNN kernels
limitations: Demonstration limited to single RISC-V accelerator; portability to other custom ISAs not discussed.
primary_theme: domain-specific compiler backend for RISC-V accelerators
